steps.content: The turmoil in the hall is growing more violent by the second. The Mania storm, on the brink of reaching its crescendo, threatens to escalate into a catastrophic event. Watching with mounting panic as the hall's entrance gradually becomes buried, Luminita grits her teeth and mutters:

steps.speaker: Luminita
steps.content: Damn it... I'll be done for if I keep waiting—
She takes a deep breath, readying herself to charge recklessly into the whirling vortex, when a tremendous crash sounds from behind her...
You breach through the wall, the red glow from your shackles piercing the swirling dust. In your hand, you clutch tightly to the journal you retrieved from the attic.

steps.speaker: Luminita
steps.content: Where have you been?! This place is about to get demolished!
Despite her grievances, Luminita has not left the two Mania creatures behind, choosing instead to remain with them amidst the chaos. You offer her a comforting pat on the shoulder.

options: I'll come to you for a house purchase later.

steps.content: Without another word, you brush past Luminita with determined steps, your gaze locked on Graves at the center of the vortex. Violent winds tear at your clothes as the storm surges around you, but you push forward and leap into the maelstrom without hesitation.

steps.speaker: Luminita
steps.content: Hey!
Luminita cries out in shock, but your figure has already vanished completely into the depths of the storm.

The ring incites and spreads Graves's darkest powers, while highly concentrated Mania howls and shrieks, resisting your approach. Flowing corruption rages past you, broken debris and sharp fragments grazing your shoulders and limbs. Yet, they fail to stop you.

Within the vortex's depths, Graves's once graceful dance has careened into chaos. Her head droops, body swaying erratically, lips moving slightly as she murmurs indecipherable words—a marionette devoid of its soul, lost to a sinister force.
Trapped in a haze, her mind struggles to grasp the sounds of the outside world. Then abruptly, a pair of hands emerges from the chaos, encircling her waist in a firm grip.
In that moment, her movements freeze. In her daze, a long-forgotten warmth touches her, as though something is pulling her back from the depths of the abyss.
You raise your hand, waving the journal you fought so desperately to recover in front of her unfocused eyes.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: I'm sorry, I accidentally ended up seeing your childhood diary and the room where you grew up.
Graves tilts her head vacantly, her gaze slowly settling on the journal.
Beneath her red skin, her features tighten slightly, confusion and bewilderment intertwined. She glances at the journal, then fixes her gaze on you.

steps.speaker: Graves
steps.content: I thought you already left. What are you doing back here?
She interrogates you in a hushed tone, both her face and tone devoid of any emotion you can detect.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: I told you I would find the real Morveth Castle after I woke up and come see you in a more complete form. See? I've kept my word.

steps.speaker: Graves
steps.content: Liar... You were clearly going back to your own place, back to somewhere without freaks. You just left me behind, because I'm a monster...
Her words are whispered as if constructing an impenetrable wall, each syllable a brick to shut you out.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: You're different. You've convinced yourself that you don't deserve any lasting connection. So you've accepted abandonment as your fate? So you're going to destroy everything now?
Graves offers no rebuttal, only pushing you away forcefully. Despite her resistance, you hold onto her even more firmly.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Actually, I'm a monster too.

steps.speaker: Graves
steps.content: You?

options: Yeah, I'm Devil in the Gray Coat.
I'm the Chief whose very name strikes terror into hearts.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: You see, I have dreams no one else can understand, I'm not scared in the slightest when I see you in this way, I can summon light spikes from my hands, and I can even rush into a storm like this to dance with you.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Aren't I quite different from what you consider "normal people"?

steps.speaker: Graves
steps.content: But... But...

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: And look over there at that real estate agent, Luminita. Would you call her normal?
You point quickly, deliberately giving her no time to think.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: She throws herself into every bit of drama, treats exorcisms like she's hawking bootleg DVDs, and not only isn't scared of phantoms—she actually haggles with them. By your standards, would she count as a monster?

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: If being "special" makes someone a monster, then everyone in this world is a monster.

steps.speaker: Graves
steps.content: So what? People will still fear me and walk away because I'm different from them.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: That's only because they refuse to admit they're monsters too. They're just as lonely and restless as you are, so they huddle together to attack a common target. It makes them feel like they're part of the "majority."

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Those children who threw stones at you were monsters too—they were just bigger cowards than you, too scared to confront their own specialness.

While your voice retains its composure, Graves becomes so bewildered by your words that she even forgets to keep dancing, her movements faltering as she clumsily stumbles on her own feet multiple times.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Everyone is special. You're just more visibly special than others, that's all. This isn't your fault, nor should it be the measure of whether you deserve to be loved.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Why must monsters only be with humans? Monsters can be with other monsters, monsters can be with anything. Just look at No. 15 and Dullahan—no matter what they've become, people still visit the castle to express their longings and honor their memory.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Love gained by conforming to everyone's beauty standards isn't necessarily genuine. True love and companionship always surpass all rules and constraints.
Graves presses her lips together and lowers her head in silence, seemingly struggling to process your words.
You hold her tighter, steadying her swaying form to prevent her from losing her balance again.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: I may have come on too strong with my points. But I remember you saying, "Graves's story isn't a good one,"—and that's even more unreasonable than what I've said.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: It's clearly a good story.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Abandoned but still searching for companions; hurt but still yearning for beauty and goodness. A Graves who tries this hard deserves it all. She shouldn't have to change herself for anyone.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: I know that no matter how many dark thoughts that damn ring has forced into her mind, the real "her" is still in there. That brave, strong Graves who never gave up on herself has been there all along. Let's bring her back out, alright?
Her shoulders tremble slightly as her gaze visibly softens. You notice the red hue of her skin beginning to fade, while the crimson patterns across her body lose their ominous depth.

steps.speaker: Graves
steps.content: If that's true... why did you turn me down?

options: I'm not ready for marriage yet...

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Who jumps straight to marriage like that? You need to spend time together first and let your feelings grow naturally, don't you think? Don't worry, there's plenty of time ahead for us.

steps.speaker: Graves
steps.content: Isn't marriage just about happily living together? What do you mean by "plenty of time ahead"?
Furrowing her brow, her eyes are clouded with confusion, like a child bewildered by the rules of the adult world.
You shake your head in resignation, letting out a soft sigh before reaching out to take her hand in yours.
[CG] [Battle Music]
You guide her to raise both hands, your fingers intertwining with hers. The shackles gradually draw together as light manifests in your palms, pulsing gently with the pressure of your grip.

Twirling and intertwining, your steps align in flawless harmony. The light spikes of the shackles slice through the lingering veil of darkness, while swirling dust scatters beneath your feet. The fractured floor silently bears witness to the cadence of your advance.
